summary: This resolution adopts the House rules from the 118th Congress for the 119th Congress, with changes to committee names and jurisdictions, limits on privileged resolutions to vacate the speakership, new electronic voting options in committee, elimination of the Office of Diversity and Inclusion, codification of various procedural orders, and immediate floor consideration of 12 specified bills on topics including immigration, abortion, and voter registration.

scores.thoughts: The resolution includes multiple provisions that directly facilitate spending reductions, such as expanding the Holman Rule to allow retrenchment of expenditures via officer reductions or compensation cuts, authorizing en bloc spending reduction amendments to appropriations bills with a dedicated spending reduction account requirement, and establishing a long-term spending point of order against net increases in direct spending exceeding $2.5 billion over specified periods. These mechanisms are designed to constrain or reduce government outlays.

The resolution contains no provisions altering tax rates, deductions, credits, or revenue collection mechanisms. One order of business references a bill on Taiwan taxation, but this is purely procedural and does not engage tax policy itself.
The resolution does not address healthcare delivery, coverage, funding, or regulation. One order of business references a bill on abortion survivors, but this is procedural only.
No provisions relate to firearms regulation, rights, or enforcement.
The resolution does not modify immigration statutes or enforcement. Several orders of business reference immigration-related bills, but these are procedural allowances only.
The resolution does not alter abortion access, funding, or restrictions. One order of business references a bill on abortion survivors, but this is procedural only.
No provisions address military funding levels, procurement, or defense policy.
The resolution does not engage environmental regulations or energy policy. One order of business references a bill on hydraulic fracturing, but this is procedural only.
No provisions modify welfare programs, entitlements, or safety-net funding.
The resolution does not alter education funding, policy, or structure. One order of business references a Title IX athletics bill, but this is procedural only.
The resolution does not change drug scheduling, enforcement, or decriminalization. One order of business references a fentanyl scheduling bill, but this is procedural only.
No provisions address sentencing, policing, or criminal justice reform.
No provisions address tariffs, trade agreements, or globalization.

Multiple spending-control mechanisms (Holman Rule expansion, spending reduction accounts, long-term direct spending point of order) are included to limit future deficits and prioritize fiscal restraint, directly engaging debt reduction priorities.
The resolution replaces gender-neutral family terms with biological-sex-specific terms in ethics rules. This is a minor, symbolic change with no direct legal effect on LGBTQ protections or rights.
No provisions address foreign assistance funding or policy.
The resolution does not alter voting procedures or election administration. One order of business references a citizenship-proof voting bill, but this is procedural only.

The resolution directs continued integration of AI tools and machine-readable legislative documents for internal House operations. This is administrative modernization with no regulatory or privacy-policy implications.
No provisions address union rights, worker protections, or employer flexibility.
No provisions address religious exemptions or anti-discrimination balances.
